title: Tanzanian Cooked Bananas
community: Kilimanjaro, Kagera, and banana-growing regions — Chagga and Haya communities
author: Mama Salima
desc: Ndizi za Kupikwa — green cooking bananas simmered in a spiced tomato and onion sauce until completely tender and starchy. The staple food of Tanzania's banana-growing regions — Kilimanjaro, Kagera, and the lake regions — where green bananas replace ugali as the primary starch.
longDesc: In Tanzania's banana-growing highlands — particularly around Kilimanjaro and in Kagera near Lake Victoria — green cooking bananas (ndizi) are as central to the diet as ugali is elsewhere. Cooked in a spiced tomato-onion sauce until completely tender, they absorb all the surrounding flavours while contributing their characteristic starchy sweetness.
steps: Peel bananas wearing gloves. Halve or cut into chunks.
Submerge in salted water immediately to prevent browning.
Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add garlic, tomatoes, and curry powder. Cook 6 minutes.
Drain bananas and add to the pot.
Add water. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer 25—30 minutes until completely tender.
chefTips: Wear gloves when peeling — latex sap stains permanently.
Keep peeled bananas in salted water — they brown rapidly.
They are done when a knife slides in without resistance.
cookingScience: Green cooking bananas are high in resistant starch and low in sugar — opposite to ripe bananas. Cooking converts some resistant starch to digestible starch, producing the characteristic tender, slightly starchy texture.
sustainabilityTips: Tanzania is one of Africa's largest banana producers.
healthBenefits: Rich in resistant starch — a prebiotic fibre.
culturalNote: Ndizi za Kupikwa are the staple of Tanzania's banana highlands — the food of Kilimanjaro's slopes where the Chagga people have cultivated hundreds of banana varieties for centuries.
